module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.Monad
public import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.PDeriv
public import Mathlib.Data.Matrix.Basic

public section

/-!
# Regular functions between affine spaces

A *regular function* from $k^σ$ to $k^τ$ is a $τ$-indexed family of polynomials in the
variables $σ$, i.e. a vector valued polynomial function. This file provides the basic
API: the Jacobian matrix, composition, the identity, and evaluation at a point.
-/

namespace MvPolynomial

variable {k : Type*} [CommRing k]
variable {σ τ ι : Type*}

variable (k σ τ) in
/-- The type of regular functions from $k^σ$ to $k^τ$. -/
abbrev RegularFunction := τ → MvPolynomial σ k

namespace RegularFunction

/-- The Jacobian of a vector valued polynomial function, viewed as a polynomial. -/
noncomputable def Jacobian (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) :
    Matrix σ τ (MvPolynomial σ k) :=
  Matrix.of fun i j => MvPolynomial.pderiv i (F j)

/-- The composition of two vector valued polynomial functions. -/
noncomputable def comp
    (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) (G : RegularFunction k τ ι) :
    RegularFunction k σ ι :=
  fun (i : ι) ↦ MvPolynomial.bind₁ F (G i)

variable (k σ) in
noncomputable def id : RegularFunction k σ σ := MvPolynomial.X

/-- The evaluation of a regular function `f` over `k` at some point `a`
with coordinates in some algebra over `k`-/
noncomputable def aeval {σ τ : Type*} {S₁ : Type*} [CommSemiring S₁] [Algebra k S₁]
    (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) : (σ → S₁) → τ → S₁ :=
  fun a t ↦ MvPolynomial.aeval a (F t)

/--`aeval` is compatible with composition of regular functions. -/
lemma comp_aeval
    {σ τ ι : Type*}
    (F : RegularFunction k σ τ) (G : RegularFunction k τ ι)
    (a : σ → k) : (F.comp G).aeval a = G.aeval (F.aeval a) := by
  ext i
  rw [aeval, comp, MvPolynomial.aeval_bind₁, ←aeval]
  rfl

end RegularFunction

end MvPolynomial

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/JacobianConjecture.lean:99, the docstring says that `F` has Jacobian determinant `1`. The declared `F` instead has determinant `-2`, as proved by `det_jacobian_F`. The determinant-one counterexample used by the theorem's proof is `G`. I also verified in Lean that `(F ℚ).Jacobian.det ≠ 1`. This is an incidental use-site documentation error, not a defect in the reviewed library definitions or the theorem statement.
findings.source_evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobian_conjecture, section “Counterexample for n > 2”, gives exactly the polynomial tuple declared as `F` and states that its determinant is −2. The original announcement https://x.com/__alpoge__/status/2079028340955197566 likewise explicitly says “has jacobian determinant -2”.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `F` with `G` in the docstring's determinant-one counterexample paragraph.

reformulations.difference: The definition stores a family of formal polynomials rather than an extensional function on the base ring's points.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Polynomial families correspond bijectively to pullback algebra homomorphisms `MvPolynomial τ k →ₐ[k] MvPolynomial σ k`: send F to `MvPolynomial.aeval F`, and recover F from the images of the variables. This is the standard affine-space morphism description, also reflected in Mathlib's `AffineSpace.homOverEquiv` and `SpecIso`. I proved this algebra-homomorphism equivalence and, over infinite integral domains, the iff between polynomial-family equality and equality of evaluated functions. Finite-field evaluation alone is not faithful, but the definition correctly retains the formal morphism; its characteristic-zero use sites do not confuse these notions.

reformulations.difference: Rows index input variables and columns index output coordinates, so the matrix is the transpose of the output-row Jacobian displayed in the conjecture's source.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This is an explicitly recognized Jacobian convention, not a different derivative. Mathlib's `Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation.jacobiMatrix_apply` uses the same variable-row convention. I proved agreement with that Mathlib matrix when the variable selection is the identity, and proved that the determinant-unit condition is equivalent to the condition for the output-row matrix using `Matrix.det_transpose`. Every conjecture use here takes the square determinant, so its mathematical condition is unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a nonzero constant Jacobian determinant and a polynomial inverse as a function. Lean uses `IsUnit` in the polynomial ring and two polynomial-family composition identities; `F.comp G` evaluates as `G ∘ F`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Over a characteristic-zero field, polynomial units are exactly nonzero constants. Evaluation respects the diagrammatic composition order, and polynomial evaluation is faithful over an infinite field, so the two formal composition identities are equivalent to the two pointwise inverse identities. Together with determinant invariance under transposition, these give the source statement exactly. The complete iff is proved as `ReviewUse.jc_iff_source` in `/workspace/review/use_sites.lean`, without `sorryAx`.
